notice: Political identity and documented external relationships, separate from territory geometry and current administrative control. Anchors reference existing research locations; none establish a capital, dependency boundary or new playable faction.

identities.name: PONTUS
identities.confidence: high for Mithridatid identity; existing scenario extent provisional
identities.notes: Existing faction retained. Pontus is the conventional retrospective name, not a proven contemporary royal title. This researched display anchor does not authorize a capital or expansion to later Mithridatid borders.

identities.name: RHODIANS
identities.confidence: high for identity; mainland extent provisional
identities.notes: Alliance with Ptolemy does not make Rhodes an Egyptian possession. Diodorus 20.99.3 records autonomy in the 304 settlement; it is not a 278 boundary survey. Later post-188 BCE mainland expansion is not projected into 278 BCE.

identities.name: LYDIA
identities.confidence: high for Seleucid Sardis; provincial limits provisional
identities.notes: Show a Lydian regional identity under Seleucid administration, not a restored independent kingdom of Croesus. No provincial boundary or office-holder is invented.

identities.name: CAPPADOCIA
identities.confidence: high for Ariarathid identity; autonomy and allegiance disputed
identities.notes: Early Ariarathid chronology and degree of autonomy are poorly resolved. Do not assert a fully independent later kingdom or certain client status. Existing territorial colour remains a separate reconstruction.

identities.name: PTOLEMAIC POSSESSIONS
identities.confidence: high for coastal activity; exact 278 extent provisional
identities.notes: Display on land already assigned to Ptolemaic Egypt. Do not fill the Side gap by extending an unsupported polygon. Later third-century evidence is not an exact 278 BCE frontier.

identities.name: MILETUS
identities.confidence: attested association in 279/278; form and extent of control provisional
identities.notes: Dated royal benefaction supports a Ptolemaic relationship; it alone does not survey a Milesian chora or prove every aspect of exclusive sovereignty. Existing Seleucid envelope mismatch is documented, not silently repainted.

identities.name: SIDE
identities.confidence: regional Ptolemaic/Seleucid activity attested; exact city control in 278 unresolved
identities.notes: Current political raster leaves the approved Side point unassigned. This is an evidence/data gap, not neutral diplomacy. Do not infer a sovereign boundary from later coins or regional influence.
